verdicts.reason: A opens on a left-side block of legal fine print set as large as secondary copy, which pulls the eye before the headline. The logo and can are tiny, and the sale ribbon is a scrap stuck under the headline. B reads left to right: product, then headline, then CTA. Its flaws are legal text nearly as heavy as a subhead and a ribbon shrunk to a tiny tag above the CTA.

A has a clean one-line headline but drops the product can and the SOLSTICE logo, so brand fidelity is lost. Its legal line is the second-largest text, and the ribbon is a tiny sliver over the CTA. B keeps the product, the logo and a readable CTA, but leads with an oversized legal-copy block on the left and leaves the ribbon tiny and orphaned under the headline.

A has the same flaws as before: a prominent legal paragraph on the left, a near-invisible logo and product, and a ribbon tucked awkwardly under the headline. B has a clear product → headline → CTA flow. Its weak points are a short 'last longer' second line and legal text set too large under the headline.

B breaks the hierarchy: the 'Claim the Deal' button is shrunk to a tiny pill in the top-right corner while the 'LONGEST DAY SALE' ribbon below it outweighs it. The headline ends on an orphaned 'longer', the large legal copy crowds the bottom, and the product is cramped at the top edge. A still overweights the legal block on the left but has a clear, prominent CTA and a readable headline.
